title: Combatting Gerrymandering with Ranked Choice Voting: an Experimental Analysis of Multi-member Districts in the United States
source_inventory_policy: Source-curated inventory for the theoretical Lemma C.1 / Proposition 1 dashboard surface. Empirical redistricting and simulation claims are intentionally out of theorem scope.

paper_pav_score.statement: Paper object for the `lambda_PAV` committee-score comparison in Proposition 1.
paper_pav_score.source_note: Source evidence: main text defines party seat share by the PAV/Thiele min-argmax formula at source.txt:425-456; Appendix Lemma C.1 states the same min-argmax, the interval y_R(M+1)-1 <= ell < y_R(M+1), and the adjacent marginal conditions at source.txt:3661-3715.

paper_pav_seat_score.statement: - Paper PAV objective over possible Republican seat counts: `y_R * sum_{i=1}^{n_R} lambda_PAV(i) + (1 - y_R) * sum_{i=1}^{M - n_R} lambda_PAV(i)`.
paper_pav_seat_score.source_note: Source evidence: main text defines party seat share by the PAV/Thiele min-argmax formula at source.txt:425-456; Appendix Lemma C.1 states the same min-argmax, the interval y_R(M+1)-1 <= ell < y_R(M+1), and the adjacent marginal conditions at source.txt:3661-3715.

paper_pav_min_argmax.statement: - Paper selector for `n_R(y_R, lambda_PAV)`: the smallest seat count maximizing the PAV objective among seat counts from `0` to `M`.
paper_pav_min_argmax.source_note: Source evidence: main text defines party seat share by the PAV/Thiele min-argmax formula at source.txt:425-456; Appendix Lemma C.1 states the same min-argmax, the interval y_R(M+1)-1 <= ell < y_R(M+1), and the adjacent marginal conditions at source.txt:3661-3715.

paper_pav_marginal_conditions.statement: - Paper proof inequalities from Lemma C.1 after clearing positive denominators. For a chosen Republican seat count `n_R`, the previous chosen Republican seat has strictly larger PAV marginal value than the next Democratic seat, and the next Republican seat has no larger PAV marginal value than the previous Democratic seat.
paper_pav_marginal_conditions.source_note: Source evidence: main text defines party seat share by the PAV/Thiele min-argmax formula at source.txt:425-456; Appendix Lemma C.1 states the same min-argmax, the interval y_R(M+1)-1 <= ell < y_R(M+1), and the adjacent marginal conditions at source.txt:3661-3715.

paper_pav_seat_interval.statement: - Paper interval characterization from Lemma C.1: `y_R (M + 1) - 1 <= n_R < y_R (M + 1)`.
paper_pav_seat_interval.source_location: Appendix Lemma C.1 source.txt:3661-3694; Proposition 1 source.txt:3740-3744
paper_pav_seat_interval.source_note: Source evidence: main text defines party seat share by the PAV/Thiele min-argmax formula at source.txt:425-456; Appendix Lemma C.1 states the same min-argmax, the interval y_R(M+1)-1 <= ell < y_R(M+1), and the adjacent marginal conditions at source.txt:3661-3715.

paper_seat_share_rounded.statement: - Paper formula target for Proposition 1: a party's seat count is one of the floor or ceiling of party vote share times the number of seats.
paper_seat_share_rounded.source_location: Appendix Lemma C.1 source.txt:3661-3694; Proposition 1 source.txt:3740-3744
paper_seat_share_rounded.source_note: Source evidence: main text defines party seat share by the PAV/Thiele min-argmax formula at source.txt:425-456; Appendix Lemma C.1 states the same min-argmax, the interval y_R(M+1)-1 <= ell < y_R(M+1), and the adjacent marginal conditions at source.txt:3661-3715.

paper_stv_solid_coalition_party_trace_is.statement: Under the solid-coalition assumption, votes can transfer from a candidate of one party to a candidate of the other party only after candidates from the sending party have been exhausted; before party exhaustion, party voters give no active support to outside-party candidates.
paper_stv_solid_coalition_party_trace_is.source_location: Proposition 1 proof source.txt:3769-3778; separate-process step source.txt:3818-3824
paper_stv_solid_coalition_party_trace_is.source_note: Source evidence: the proof says cross-party transfer can occur only if candidates from the sending party have been exhausted, because voters rank all same-party candidates above all other-party candidates; it then uses that fact to carry out the initial STV rounds separately for each party.

paper_stv_solid_coalition_quota_witness_.statement: Paper STV quota-witness consequence used by the quota arithmetic bridge.
paper_stv_solid_coalition_quota_witness_.source_note: Source evidence: Proposition 1 states the STV/PAV rounded-seat conclusion at source.txt:3740-3744; the appendix proof introduces the Droop quota, separate same-party quota processes, quota-capacity argument, and final STV lower/upper bounds at source.txt:3748-3868.

paper_proposition1_from_generated_filled.statement: Proposition 1 theoretical endpoint: for a two-party election under the solid-coalition STV/PAV setup, the generated filled-seat fractional STV outcome and the PAV min-argmax seat count are both rounded party vote shares.
paper_proposition1_from_generated_filled.source_note: Source evidence: Proposition 1 states the STV/PAV rounded-seat conclusion; the appendix proof uses solid coalitions, Droop quota accounting, separate party STV processes, and final STV lower/upper bounds.
